title: 1D Beam - Bending Analysis (FEM)
desc.equation: Beam bending by Euler-Bernoulli theory: w(x) is the transverse deflection, E(x) Young's modulus, I(x) the moment of inertia and q(x) the distributed load:
desc.props: E and I are constant or vary along x (linearly or parabolically) according to the properties selector.
desc.domain: Beam of length L divided into nₑ beam elements of uniform size:
desc.bc.intro: Supports according to the selector (θ = w' is the rotation); the moment and shear conditions at the supports are natural in the formulation:
desc.bc.cantilever: Cantilever (fixed at x = 0, free end at x = L):
desc.bc.fs: Propped cantilever (fixed at x = 0, simple support at x = L):
desc.load.intro: Available loads (q is the magnitude entered):
desc.load.linear: Linear, from q at x = 0 to q/2 at x = L:
desc.load.triangular: Triangular, with peak q at the center and zero at the ends:
desc.load.point: Point load, force P = qL at the center, approximated by a narrow Gaussian distribution:
desc.method: Finite Element Method with Euler-Bernoulli beam elements (cubic Hermite shape functions, two degrees of freedom per node: w and θ). Properties and load evaluated as the average of the nodal values in each element. Bending moment M = −EI w'' and shear force V = −EI w''' obtained from the derivatives of the shape functions and averaged at the nodes.
desc.reference: For constant EI and uniform load q (Mechanics of Materials):
desc.reference.note: In the other cases (propped cantilever, other loads or variable properties) the simulation shows only the numerical result.
note.analytical_only: Available only for constant properties and uniform load
